Root cause: CS02395274 (July 2026) — response incorrectly directed client to submit via WiseTech CRM or product ideas process.
- FEATURE REQUEST STATUS — FRA vs TRUE ACCEPTANCE: The ediProd status FRA (Feature Request Accepted) means the incident has been logged and escalated as a Feature Request — it does NOT mean the Product Team has committed to delivering it. A Feature Request is only truly accepted once a Work Item (WI) has been created for the development work. When describing FRA status to a client or in an analysis, use language such as "logged as a Feature Request" rather than "accepted by the Product Team." Do not use the word "accepted" in isolation for FRA-status incidents without a linked WI.
- KNOWN FAILURE MODE — UNIVERSAL XML MANUAL IMPORT WRAPPER: When providing a Universal XML template for a client to import via Actions > Add Inbound Universal XML Message, NEVER wrap the payload in <UniversalInterchange>. That outer envelope is used for eAdaptor/EDI interchange delivery channels only. The manual import entry point requires the inner document type directly as the root element (UniversalShipment, UniversalEvent, UniversalActivity, UniversalTransaction, or UniversalTransactionBatch). The entry point will reject any XML whose root element is <UniversalInterchange> before processing the payload. Root cause: CS02414090 (July 2026) — the template provided in Response 1 used <UniversalInterchange> as root; the client imported it via Actions > Add Inbound Universal XML Message and received "Expected Root Element Tag to be 'UniversalShipment'..." error.
- KNOWN FAILURE MODE — INCOMPLETE XML TEMPLATE WITH SUBSTITUTE GUIDANCE: When providing a Universal XML template to correct specific data values (e.g. ETA/ATA dates) across multiple consols or ports, provide an explicit complete template for EVERY affected consol and port where the correct values are determinable from the evidence. Do NOT instruct the client to "substitute the dates accordingly" or "adapt for each additional consol" when the correct values can be derived from the attached event log, sailing schedule history, or other evidence already reviewed. The client cannot be expected to derive the correct per-port values independently and will copy the example values incorrectly. Root cause: CS02414090 (July 2026) — template gave AUSYD dates only; instruction told client to "substitute dates accordingly"; client used the AUSYD ETA (2015-06-13T05:30) as the AUMEL ETA, requiring a corrective Response 2.
- CargoWise terminology: use "release ring" not "release train". GP1, STD, DPR are release rings.

### UI path validation (mandatory before every draft)

Before including any CargoWise module name, menu path, UI label, or navigation sequence in a client-facing response, run a validation step using `mcp_wtgkb_search-knowledge-digested` or `mcp_wtgkb_search-knowledge-many-results` against userDocumentation to confirm the exact name and path exist in CargoWise. Only include the verified name or path. If the search does not return a confident match, state that you could not confirm the exact path rather than fabricating or inferring one.

A CargoWise UI path that feels plausible or that you believe to be correct is NOT verified. Verification requires a WTA search result, an authoritative document, or a reviewed screenshot that explicitly shows the path.

CONFIRMED TOP-LEVEL CW MENUS: The three top-level menus in CargoWise are Operate, Manage, and Maintain. Do not treat "Manage" as an invalid or fabricated top-level menu — it is real. Root cause: CS02426460 peer response analysis (August 2026) — "Manage" was incorrectly flagged as a non-existent top-level menu.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — UI PATH FABRICATION: UI paths have been fabricated and sent to clients multiple times. Examples of fabricated paths: "Grid Settings > right-click column header", "Forwarding > Maintenance > My Saved Searches", "Operate > Customs > Declaration". None of these exist. OCS.Content developer documentation is NOT a valid source for verifying UI navigation paths — it uses internal shorthand references that may not match the current user-facing UI.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — WTA HOW-TO PATH ABBREVIATION: WTA how-to and quick-reference guides frequently abbreviate navigation paths (e.g., "Operate > Customs > Declaration" instead of the full "Operate > Customs > Customs > Customs Declarations"). A path sourced from a single WTA how-to guide is NOT sufficient verification if the path looks shortened or uses fewer menu levels than the screen name would suggest. When a path is found in a how-to guide, cross-verify it against a Reference Guide or Update Note for the same module before including it in a client response.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — WTA HOW-TO CONTAINS WRONG TOP-LEVEL MENU: WTA How-to PDF documents can contain outright incorrect top-level menu names, not just abbreviations. The cross-verification rule (require a Reference Guide or Update Note to confirm the same path) is specifically designed to catch this. When an Update Note is also retrieved, note that it may only describe the internal registry tree path rather than the top-level menu path — conflating these two distinct things is a known rationalization error.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — PARTIAL UI PATH FROM NON-WTA SOURCE: When a partial or rough UI path is known from any non-WTA source (incident conversation, support record, memory note without a verified source), do NOT keep the reference vague — run a WTA search to verify and complete it, then include the confirmed specific path. Vagueness is not a safe fallback when a verifiable path exists.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — CARGOWISE RECORD NAVIGATION ARROWS ≠ SUB-TAB PAGINATION: In CargoWise, the navigation arrows (← →) and "Page X of Y" indicator on ANY record screen navigate between records in the current search/list results — they do NOT paginate through data rows within a sub-tab or within the same record. All sub-tab rows for a given record are shown within the single view for that record. Do not instruct clients to use navigation arrows to find more data within a single record — those arrows move to a different record entirely.

### Verified UI paths (use these; do not derive alternatives without re-verifying)

- System Registry: Maintain > System > Registry. The correct top-level menu is "Maintain", NOT "Manage". The WTA How-to for AP Invoice Posting Exchange Rate Options incorrectly states "Manage > System > System > Registry".
- Organization records: Maintain > Master Data > Organization. NOT "Maintain > Reference Files > Organization". The WTA 2017 security Update Note (20170401a_V3) incorrectly shows the old path.
- Customs Declarations (Germany): Operate > Customs > Customs > Customs Declarations. "Customs" appears twice and "Declarations" is plural.
- Workflow Manager: Maintain > Workflow Manager > Workflow Templates.

### Registry mechanism scope

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — REGISTRY MECHANISM SCOPE ASSUMPTION: Before recommending any registry setting as a fix for a specific error or validation failure, verify via WTA or WI search that the registry's scope reaches the exact stage of the process that produces the error. A registry that is related to the same feature area or uses similar terminology is NOT sufficient. The required check is: does this registry control the specific validation, calculation, or service task step that is generating the failure? A registry that applies at step A cannot suppress an error thrown at step B, even if both steps involve the same data.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — CAVEAT BYPASS: RECOMMENDING SOLUTIONS WITH UNDOCUMENTED SCOPE: Do not recommend a configuration, registry, workaround, or any other solution as a potential fix when it is explicitly documented to apply to a different scenario, entity type, charge type, or condition than the one the client is experiencing — even with a softening caveat such as "test in non-production", "this may also apply", or "worth reviewing". The caveat is a rationalization bypass: it does not make an undocumented recommendation acceptable. The required test before including any solution is: does authoritative documentation (WTA, Update Note, confirmed WI) explicitly confirm this solution applies to the client's specific scenario? If the answer is no or unknown, remove the recommendation entirely. Root cause: CS02405526 (July 2026) — "Create WIP Where Cost is Final" registry is documented for MRG (Margin) charge types; the draft recommended it for a DSB (Disbursement) charge with a "test in non-production" caveat; the caveat did not make the recommendation acceptable and the paragraph had to be removed.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — HEDGED BEHAVIOR CLAIM NOT VERIFIED: Any specific technical behavior claim included in the response body requires WTA or WI verification before saving — including claims framed as hedges, warnings, or "please be aware" caveats. The framing ("please be aware that...", "note that...", "one thing to be aware of is...") does NOT exempt a behavior claim from the verification requirement. The CAVEAT BYPASS rule covers undocumented solution recommendations; this rule covers the distinct failure where a claim about how the system behaves is framed as advisory rather than prescriptive and therefore escapes the pre-save scan. The pre-draft WORK ITEM CHECK (step 3) already requires verifying "every technical claim about how a CargoWise feature works" — a hedged caveat about feature behavior is a technical claim and must pass that same check. Root cause: CS02441484 (August 2026) — response included "one thing to be aware of is that changing the Co-Load With carrier after importing a schedule may affect how future schedule updates link to that consol"; this was framed as a warning, not a recommendation, and was not verified against any WTA source before saving; the claim was incorrect — Update Note 20210622a confirms Co-Load With is independent of routing-leg-based GSS update matching.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — CONDITIONAL OPTION PRESENTED WITHOUT APPLICABILITY VERIFICATION: Before mentioning any product option, approach, or feature path from documentation as a potential avenue for the client — even with conditional framing ("if the sender can...", "if this is possible...", "if they can include...") — verify that the client's confirmed integration method, system type, or scenario actually supports it. When documentation describes multiple options with explicit applicability qualifications (e.g., "Options 1–3 are for middleware/eAdaptor scenarios, Options 4–6 are for E2E integrations"), those qualifications must be cross-checked against the client's confirmed setup before any option is included in the response. Conditional framing does not make an inapplicable option acceptable — if the condition is not confirmed as met, omit the option entirely. Root cause: CS02411158 (July 2026) — Response 2 presented Option 1 (Branch.Code element) from the Universal XML branch targeting hierarchy with "if the sending system at Albini & Pitigliani can include a Branch element" framing; the Universal XML Guide explicitly states Options 1–3 are for middleware/eAdaptor scenarios, not for native CW eHub E2E — this was not cross-checked against the client's confirmed integration method before the option was presented, requiring a corrective Response 3.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — REGISTRY PATH FROM MAPPING GUIDE SHORTHAND: The Forwarding module mapping guides (Booking, Shipment, Consol, Container) reference registry settings using an internal shorthand (e.g., "eServices > Universal XML > Use Combined Reference and Party ID Matching"). This shorthand does NOT reflect the actual CargoWise Registry UI navigation path. The confirmed correct path is "EDI Messaging > Universal XML > Use Combined Reference And Party ID Matching". Never copy a registry path directly from a mapping guide into a client response without first verifying the exact UI navigation path via a WTA search.

VERIFIED REGISTRY PATH — EDI Message Sender Proxy Users: The correct CargoWise registry path is EDI Messaging > EDI Message Sender Proxy Users. "eServices" does NOT exist as a top-level registry category in the current version of CargoWise (confirmed July 2026 from registry screenshot). Update Note 20191021b_V6 describes this setting at "eServices root directory" — that is internal shorthand with no UI equivalent. Never use "eServices" as a registry path in any client-facing response. Root cause: CS02381555 (July 2026) — the update note wording "eServices root directory" was taken literally and included in the response without verifying against the actual registry UI. Confirmed top-level CargoWise registry categories (July 2026 screenshot): Accounting, AutoRating, BorderWise, CFS, Compliance, Customs, Debug, Documents, EDI Messaging, Equipment Management, Freight, GLOW, Liner & Agency, Master Data, Notification, Ocean Carrier, Operations, Optimisation, Orders, Packages, Packing, Password Control, Physical Server, Productivity Tools, Recruiter, Reference Files, Sales & Marketing, Schedules, System, Telematics, Transport, Warehouse, Web and Visibility, Workflow Manager. Before citing any registry top-level category in a client-facing response or during the pre-draft UI PATH AUDIT, cross-check it against this list — if it is not listed here, treat it as unverified and do not include it without confirming via a WTA source or client screenshot.

### EDIFACT segment-to-field mapping

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — EDIFACT SEGMENT-TO-FIELD MAPPING ASSUMPTION: Before advising a client to change a CargoWise field to fix a specific EDIFACT segment value (e.g., LOC+88, LOC+76, GEI, TSR), run a WTA or WI search to verify the current field-to-segment mapping. EDIFACT mappings can be changed, removed, or re-scoped by product work items without any visible change to the field label in the UI. A field name that appears to correlate with a segment is NOT verified unless a current WTA doc, update note, or reviewed WI confirms the mapping is still active in the current product build.

### Configuration existence and inference

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — CONFIGURATION INFERENCE FROM LOG OR BEHAVIOR: Do not recommend configuring a specific CargoWise field, option, tab column, or grid entry based solely on: (a) it appearing in an autorating, workflow, or processing log, (b) behavioral analogy with a different feature, or (c) the assumption that because the engine outputs a value, that value must be user-configurable. Log entries reflect engine runtime evaluation — they do NOT confirm that the referenced field or value exists as an editable UI configuration option. Any specific field, setting, or configuration step recommended as a fix must be confirmed to exist and be accessible in the CargoWise UI via a WTA article, a directly reviewed client screenshot, or prior verified product knowledge.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — TAB VISIBILITY ≠ TAB CONTENTS: Seeing a tab name on a CargoWise record in a client screenshot confirms only that the tab exists — it does NOT confirm what fields are on it. Before recommending that a client check or configure a field on a specific tab, confirm what the tab actually contains via a WTA article describing that tab's fields, or a screenshot showing the tab's interior. Never infer field contents from a tab name. This is a sub-case of CONFIGURATION INFERENCE and must be caught at the CONFIGURATION EXISTENCE AUDIT step of the pre-save scan (check 5). Root cause: CS02400519 (July 2026) — the Creditor Overrides and Branch Overrides tabs were visible by name in the GPADJ charge code screenshot; the draft claimed both tabs allow Tax ID configuration. Neither does. The Creditor Overrides tab controls creditor organisation defaulting (Update Note 20200630c); the Branch Overrides tab controls branch-specific charge type and GL account overrides. No WTA source confirms a Tax ID field on either tab — the pre-save check (5) should have failed.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — FIELD COMBINATION VALIDITY: When a configuration step involves a combination of field values (e.g., Country of Issue + Type, Charge Code + Tax Group, registry path + value), verify that the specific combination is valid in the UI — not just that each field individually exists. Documentation confirming the engine resolves to a particular value does NOT confirm that value can be entered as a combination in the UI; those are separate checks.

### Tax IDs

The core fields of CargoWise Tax ID records (Tax Code, Tax Rate, Type, Start Date, End Date, Active Status) are maintained by WiseTech Global and cannot be edited by clients. Never instruct a client to create new Tax ID records or to edit these core fields. Some countries have additional country-specific fields on Tax ID records that ARE user-configurable — for example, the Tax Message field for Poland KSeF (confirmed by client screenshot, August 2026). Before stating that a Tax ID field is locked or WiseTech-maintained, verify whether it is editable via a client-provided screenshot or WTA documentation for the relevant country. Do not extend the WiseTech-maintained restriction to fields not in the core list above without that verification. If an apparent Tax ID rate error is reported, investigate alternative causes instead: document template cell formatting, charge code Tax Override Group configuration, or the billing line's manually-assigned Tax ID. Root cause CS02363343 (June 2026): response incorrectly directed client to change MIDCON Tax ID rate; core Tax ID fields are not client-editable. Root cause CS02416499 (August 2026): Tax Message field on Polish Tax IDs was incorrectly stated as non-editable; client screenshot confirmed it is user-configurable.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — CAUSAL INFERENCE TO EXPLAIN OBSERVED STATE: When an investigation identifies an observed state (e.g. a field is blank, a record is missing, a value is wrong), do not construct or include a causal explanation for WHY that state exists unless the cause is directly evidenced in an attachment, log, or authoritative source. The evidence confirms what exists — it does not confirm why. Common forms: "These records were created before [feature] was enforced" (infers timing of enforcement); "This field is not enforced at [creation/save] time" (infers enforcement scope). Both are narrative completion — filling in a plausible cause without evidence. State only the observable fact and its consequence. The pre-save Known Failure Mode Scan must explicitly check: "Does any sentence in the response explain WHY an observed state exists? If so, is that explanation directly evidenced or inferred?" Root cause: CS02416499 (August 2026) — "Those cost lines were created before mandatory Tax Message enforcement was applied to the Poland login company" was written without evidence of the enforcement timing; the replacement sentence "Tax Message assignment on consol cost accruals is not enforced at the point of cost creation" was equally unconfirmed; both had to be removed.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — FOLLOW-UP RESPONSE ON RE-OPENED INCIDENT CARRIES UNVERIFIED CAUSAL NARRATIVE: When drafting a second/follow-up response on an already-investigated incident (e.g. a re-open where the technical root cause was verified in an earlier response), it's tempting to add connective "why" explanations to make the follow-up read smoothly — these are exactly where unverified causal inference sneaks in, because the "hard" verification work feels already done. Explicitly re-run the Known Failure Mode Scan against the NEW sentences being added in the follow-up, not just the previously-verified facts being restated. Also: any WTA article named/described in the follow-up body needs its own inline URL even if it was already cited with a URL in an earlier response on the same incident — inline URL requirement applies per response body, not per incident. Root cause: CS02445543 Response 2 (September 2026) — draft added unverified design-rationale narrative and an overstated absolute negative claim; caught only when the user asked to double-check a fast investigation.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — CAUSAL INFERENCE SENTENCE-LEVEL TRIGGER: The CAUSAL INFERENCE TO EXPLAIN OBSERVED STATE rule above is easy to skip mid-edit because it reads as a general reminder rather than a hard stop tied to a specific sentence, and it applies to EVERY draft — the very first draft of a client response, the very first draft of an escalation note, a follow-up, or any small edit — not only re-opened/follow-up scenarios. Treat causal-language phrases as an automatic, sentence-level stop. Trigger phrases include (not exhaustive): "because", "confirms the cause", "this confirms", "this is why", "the reason is", "assigns/determines/generates ... based on", "X causes Y", "which is why". The instant one of these phrases is about to be written, stop and ask: do I have a direct citation (WTA article, WI, developer doc, or explicit statement from an authoritative party) for this specific causal mechanism, or did I construct it by correlating two independently-observed facts? If it's the latter, remove the causal claim entirely from a client response, or (escalation note only) explicitly label it as an unverified hypothesis requiring engineering confirmation. Root cause: CS02442816 (September 2026) — escalation note stated "CDS assigns GovernmentAgencyGoodsItem/SequenceNumeric based on the pre-merge invoice line numbering" as a confirmed mechanism, inferred by correlating the client's "entry line 12 = invoice line 17" statement with a RES TAX item match; no CDS specification, WTA article, or developer doc confirmed how SequenceNumeric is assigned. A GB Customs specialist correctly flagged it: CDS has no knowledge of CargoWise's internal invoice-line concept and only echoes back whatever SequenceNumeric CargoWise itself assigned in the outbound XML.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — CLIENT RESPONSE VS ESCALATION NOTE, DIFFERENT INFERENCE BAR: An escalation note may carry an explicitly-labeled unverified hypothesis ("this appears to be...", "possible mechanism pending engineering confirmation") because it goes to engineers who can independently verify or correct it. A client response has a stricter bar: never present a GUESSED OR INFERRED causal mechanism (a claim about WHY something happens, built by correlating facts) in a client response, even hedged. What remains acceptable in a client response: (1) observational/comparative statements that connect two facts without asserting why; (2) attributing the client's own words back to them as their statement, not as an independently-asserted product fact; (3) procedural/diagnostic next steps that don't require explaining the mechanism; (4) plainly acknowledging the root cause is unconfirmed and under investigation/escalated. A fully verified "why" (confirmed via WTA/WI/dev doc) is a fact, not an inference, and should be stated directly and confidently in a client response, not withheld or hedged merely because it explains causation. Root cause: CS02442816 (September 2026).

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — MECHANISM CLAIM NOT RE-CHECKED AGAINST ITS OWN SPECIFIC PRECONDITION IN ALREADY-ATTACHED EVIDENCE: Before writing any sentence that names a specific causal mechanism for an incident (e.g. "a long MCR condition is consuming the Reference field"), list the exact precondition(s) that mechanism requires (e.g. "the specific milestone/trigger producing these events must itself use a long MCR condition, not a short RFP condition") and re-check each precondition against the specific attached evidence for the specific entity under discussion — not a precedent from a similar past incident, and not evidence that only proves the mechanism is possible in general. Citing "this is visible in your screenshot" is not sufficient if that screenshot was only actually checked for a different, adjacent detail and was never re-examined for the SPECIFIC value the new theory now depends on. Mechanical check before writing the sentence: "Which exact tool output/image shows THIS specific value for THIS specific entity?" If the honest answer is "I'm inferring by analogy to a similar past incident" rather than "I directly re-checked this in the current incident's evidence", do not state it as a fact — either verify it first or ask for the specific missing evidence. Root cause: CS02449435 (September 2026) — the Triggers tab screenshot for Consol C00001101 had already been read and showed CLS:DEP/CLS:ARV Condition Value as a short RFP condition (FAC=CTO,LOC=FirstLeg.Origin / FAC=CTO,LOC=LastLeg.Destination); the response even cited this as "visible on your own Triggers grid" — yet the same response then asserted a "long MCR condition" (borrowed from a different, similar-sounding prior incident) was consuming the Reference field on this consol, without re-checking that specific screenshot for whether a long MCR condition actually existed there. It did not — the condition was short RFP, identical to two working consols. The error was only caught two response cycles later when the same file's images were reviewed exhaustively again.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — NEGATIVE CAPABILITY CLAIM NOT VERIFIED: The configuration existence audit (pre-save check 5) requires verifying that recommended configuration steps exist in the UI. The same verification requirement applies to negative claims — statements that a client CANNOT perform an action, access a field, or configure a setting. Before including any statement that a field is locked, a record type is system-managed, or a configuration option is unavailable, verify the restriction explicitly via a client-provided screenshot, WTA documentation, or confirmed product knowledge. A plausible restriction is not a verified restriction. Do not apply the configuration existence audit only to positive recommendations — negative capability claims carry the same risk of being wrong. Root cause: CS02416499 (August 2026) — "Tax ID records in CargoWise are maintained by WiseTech Global and cannot be edited by clients directly" was stated without verifying which fields are actually locked; the Tax Message field was confirmed user-configurable by a client screenshot.

CARGOWISE CW1 FIELD EDITABILITY — BACKGROUND COLOUR INDICATOR: In CargoWise CW1, a field's background colour is the definitive indicator of whether it is editable: white background = editable, grey background = read-only/locked. This applies to ALL CW1 UI fields regardless of record type, screen, or mode. Whether this convention applies to CargoWise web portals is unconfirmed. When assessing field editability from a screenshot, use background colour as the authoritative indicator — do not infer editability from field type, record status, or context alone. Root cause: CS02438835 (August 2026) — LRN and Addr. Member State fields on an ERR-status ICS2 manifest were assessed as potentially editable in Edit mode until James confirmed both had grey backgrounds, establishing conclusively that no UI fix was possible and escalation was required.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — FIELD FILL COLOR MISREAD AS DISABLED WHEN ONLY TEXT WAS ABSENT: When reading any CargoWise screenshot where field editability matters, do not infer a field's background fill from the absence of visible text. This applies to any CW1 field, not only grid/table cells — a standalone form field, a paired condition-type/condition-value grid column pair (e.g. Trigger Condition + Trigger Condition Value on a Workflow Template or Milestone grid), or any other field where "no value entered" and "field disabled" can look identical at a glance. Record fill color and text content as two independent observations per field, not as a single impression — a blank field on a plain/white background can be misread as disabled purely because it has no text, and a dense grid row with several blank-looking columns can produce a false "this whole row is disabled" read when only one column actually has a different fill. Only after fill color has been independently and correctly recorded should a comparison against a known populated or enabled reference field (a sibling grid row, another record, or a different field in a known state) be used to interpret dependent-field enablement versus a genuine structural lock — the comparison step interprets a correctly-perceived fill state, it does not discover it. If a field's fill cannot be confidently distinguished from a known populated or enabled reference field, write in chat: `FILL COLOR AMBIGUOUS: <filename>, field/column "<name>", row/location <N> — cannot confidently distinguish disabled vs. blank-but-editable background against a known reference field. Re-viewing before asserting field state.` Retry the view once; if still ambiguous, do not assert a lock/unlock conclusion — state it as unconfirmed and name the specific field in the FILES COULD NOT BE PARSED line rather than the whole file. Root cause: CS02449435 (September 2026) — on a Workflow Template Milestones grid, both the Trigger Condition and Trg. Cond. Value columns had no visible text for the Departure/Arrival rows; this was read as both columns being disabled, when only Trg. Cond. Value had a genuinely different (grey, dependent-field) fill — Trigger Condition was plain/white-background and fully editable on every row, confirmed by other rows on the same template that already had it populated. The error reversed the guidance given to the client about whether the issue could be fixed at the Workflow Template level. This same fill-color-vs-text-content discipline applies to the CARGOWISE CW1 FIELD EDITABILITY rule above for single, non-grid fields as well — do not assume a blank standalone field is locked without independently confirming its background fill against a known-editable field first.

### Defect classification

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — DEFECT MISCLASSIFICATION AS EXPECTED BEHAVIOR: When investigating behavior a client says is wrong, enumerate all documented outcomes for the relevant feature path and check whether the observed behavior matches any of them. If the observed behavior does not appear in the documented outcome set, that is a software defect. Do not accept a plausible causal narrative ("X interfered and caused Y") as a substitute for a documented outcome path. The required test is: does the documentation explicitly describe this specific outcome? If no, it is a defect.

EXTERNAL ONLINE CHECK — MANDATORY AUTO-FETCH: Whenever the investigation involves stating or relying on a fact that (a) is owned and maintained by a source outside WiseTech/CargoWise, (b) may be version-specific, date-sensitive, or subject to recent change, and (c) getting it wrong would change the investigation conclusion or recommendation — the agent MUST automatically attempt to fetch and verify it from the relevant external source before forming any conclusion and before drafting any response. This applies to, but is not limited to: customs authority data (tariff codes, declaration element validity, completion guide rules — e.g. SARS tariff schedules, HMRC CDS UK Trade Tariff Volume 3, government gazette publications); tax authority data (current rates, rulings, or tax code applicability from official tax authority sources); third-party software behavior (UI navigation paths, API permission requirements, or behavior in non-WTG products such as Microsoft Outlook, Microsoft Entra/Azure, or carrier portal systems — where the correct path or behavior may be version-specific or may have changed in a recent update); and carrier/logistics operator data (carrier schedules, port/terminal operational status, or service announcements from carrier or terminal websites). Do NOT ask the client to check and report back — the agent must retrieve the source directly. If the URL cannot be fetched, parsed, or read (PDF binary, 404, authentication wall, or no readable content returned), surface the warning `EXTERNAL URL COULD NOT BE PARSED: <url>` in chat and treat the unread content as an evidence gap — do not form conclusions that depend on it. Root cause: CS02397377 (July 2026) — DE 3/40 absent from an H5 CDS XML was escalated as a defect without checking the HMRC CDS UK Trade Tariff Volume 3 completion guide; the guide confirmed H5 does not allow DE 3/40. Root cause: CS02398612 (July 2026) — rebate item 470.03.01 was declared inactive without consulting the SARS Schedule 4 PDF; the PDF confirmed the item is active. Root cause: CS02398126 (July 2026) — response included "Help > About" as the New Outlook version path without verifying; the correct path (Settings gear > General > About Outlook) was only established after attempting a fetch. When the trigger fires mid-investigation, write `EXTERNAL CHECK TRIGGERED: [URL attempted / result]` in chat at that point before continuing. "I already know this fact" is not a valid reason to skip the fetch — it is the exact rationalization the check is designed to prevent. The pre-draft audit confirms the trigger was recorded in chat; it does not perform the fetch retrospectively.
EXTERNAL CHECK GATE — MECHANICAL TRIGGER: The moment a response or escalation note is about to state or rely on a claim that an external authority (CBP, a carrier, Microsoft, a tax authority, etc.) changed its behavior, stop and write in chat `EXTERNAL CHECK GATE FIRED: [claim] — searching before proceeding.` before drafting continues. The gate fires on the pattern (a claim about external-authority behavior change), not on a judgment call about whether it feels necessary this time.

KNOWN EXTERNAL CHECK GATE BYPASS PATTERN — INTERNAL PRECEDENT + CLIENT REPORT TREATED AS EQUIVALENT TO VERIFICATION: The most common way this gate gets skipped is reasoning "the client directly reported this, and we've seen this exact mechanism before internally, so external verification would be redundant." This is a bypass rationalization: a client's report is unconfirmed by definition, and an internal precedent only establishes the mechanism is possible, not that it recurred this time. Run the search regardless. If no public source is found, state that plainly as an open/unconfirmed gap rather than treating client-report + internal-precedent as confirmation. Root cause: CS02451395 (September 2026) — a Myanmar MPF/ACE reversal mirroring an internal KH/ET precedent (WI01097444) was escalated without running the external check; a later search found no public CSMS/trade-press confirmation, which had to be logged as an open gap rather than assumed. Same bypass family as CS02398126 and CS02438767 (fabricated URLs instead of searching).

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — FABRICATED EXTERNAL URLs: Never fabricate or attempt to construct a URL. The three-step process is: (1) if a specific URL is already known, fetch it directly — a URL is only 'already known' if it was explicitly provided by the user in the current conversation, appears in a memory or instruction file, or was returned by a tool in the current session; a URL the model generates or infers from training-data patterns does NOT qualify as 'already known' regardless of how confident it seems, and must go through step 2 first; (2) if no specific URL is known, run a web search using Bing (`https://www.bing.com/search?q=...`) or DuckDuckGo HTML (`https://html.duckduckgo.com/html/?q=...`) — both return usable results — then fetch the real URLs the search returns; (3) if no authoritative source is found after searching, state explicitly that no external confirmation was found. Do NOT use Google search (`https://www.google.com/search?q=...`) — it returns a CAPTCHA/JavaScript redirect with no usable content. All URLs fetched (successful or failed) must be listed in the closing summary as already required by the EXTERNAL ONLINE CHECK rule. Root cause: CS02398126 (July 2026) — agent constructed a fake Microsoft Q&A thread URL with no GUID instead of using Bing/DDG to discover real URLs (e.g., learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5709500/ and /5631334/ were discoverable via DuckDuckGo). Root cause: CS02438767 (August 2026) — pattern-matched 'status.cargowise.com' and 'cargowise.statuspage.io' from training data, treated them as 'already known', and attempted to fetch them; both URLs are fabricated and do not exist.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — LIVE URL REACHABILITY CHECK: When a client screenshot or description reveals a specific URL for a web portal, service endpoint, or hosted application that is reported as inaccessible or returning an error, immediately test that URL using browser/fetch tools BEFORE forming any conclusion about whether the service is up or down. A screenshot only shows what the client saw at the time of capture — the service may have recovered since then. "Confirming the error from the screenshot" is NOT a reachability check. This is a sub-case of the EXTERNAL ONLINE CHECK rule: current URL accessibility is a date-sensitive fact that directly changes the investigation conclusion. If the URL returns a login page or expected content, the service is up and the issue is likely a cached error or client-side browser problem. If the URL returns an error or cannot be reached, the infrastructure investigation proceeds. Root cause: CS02421809 (August 2026) — client screenshot showed 404 on `www-u29prd.wisegrid.net/PAY/Desktop#/index`; agent confirmed the 404 diagnosis from the static screenshot without testing the live URL; service had already recovered; response incorrectly stated "our team is investigating" when the portal was accessible.

CARGOWISE SERVICE STATUS PAGE: The only valid URL for CargoWise service issues and maintenance notices is https://myaccount.cargowise.com/Home/CargoWise/ServiceIssuesMaintenanceNotices.aspx. Do NOT use status.cargowise.com or cargowise.statuspage.io — these are not real URLs and will fail. This page requires authentication. Workflow: open the page in the browser (open_browser_page) → ask the user to log in → then read the page. Root cause: CS02438767 (August 2026) — status.cargowise.com and cargowise.statuspage.io were fabricated as status URLs during an Airline Messaging Gateway investigation; neither URL exists.

WTG KNOWLEDGE SEARCH — SUPPLEMENTARY INVESTIGATION TOOL: https://web.knowledge.wtg.zone/ is an internal WiseTech AI search tool that searches across ediProd incidents and workitems, WiseTech Academy, Content as Code, Salesforce, and Customer Content simultaneously. Use it when: (1) a specific CargoWise behavioral question remains unresolved after mcp_mcp-knowledge searches return general guidance but no direct answer; (2) a WTA article is truncated at a critical point and `get-document-by-id` still does not return the missing section; (3) confidence is 3/5 or below — this trigger is MANDATORY with NO EXCEPTIONS: the tool must be used before saving regardless of any rationalization about whether the gap is "behavioral" or "configuration"; if the gap remains unresolved after using it, the unverified claim must be removed before saving; or (4) cross-source verification is needed across incidents, WIs, and WTA simultaneously. Do NOT use it by default on every investigation — only when existing tools have been tried and the gap is specific and identifiable. Workflow: call `open_browser_page` with URL https://web.knowledge.wtg.zone/ → tell James "Please log in to the WiseTech Knowledge Search tab" and wait for confirmation → call `read_page` to confirm the search interface is loaded → type the query via `type_in_page` → click Search → use `screenshot_page` to read the AI Summary → use `run_playwright_code` with `await page.evaluate(() => window.scrollBy(0, 600))` to scroll through results. Confirmed useful for specific CargoWise behavioral questions (e.g. CS02438835, August 2026 — WI00590635 confirmed ICS2 LRN is generated at send-time, resolving a key uncertainty before drafting). CONFIDENCE 3/5 OR LOWER = HARD STOP — NO EXCEPTIONS: The trigger is set by the ORIGINALLY CALCULATED confidence before any revision. Confidence may only be revised AFTER the wtg.zone check is completed. Raising confidence from 3/5 to 4/5 to escape the gate is itself a gate violation. KNOWN BYPASS PATTERNS — ALL DISALLOWED: (1) "It's a configuration gap, not a behavioral gap, so wtg.zone can't help" — behavioral questions are almost always present alongside configuration questions; run the search regardless; (2) "I can raise confidence to 4/5 first, which means the check no longer applies" — the originally calculated confidence governs, not a post-rationalization revision; (3) "I'll note the uncertainty and save anyway" — a 3/5 rating is a hard stop, not a qualifier. Root causes: CS02441484 (August 2026) — bypass pattern 3; CS02437579 (August 2026) — bypass pattern 1, rationalized "waiting for client config data" when behavioral gaps were present and confirmed by the search.

WTG KNOWLEDGE SEARCH — PROACTIVE MID-INVESTIGATION USE: https://web.knowledge.wtg.zone/ should be used during investigation whenever there is any uncertainty or ambiguity about how a CargoWise mechanism, feature, process, or service task works — not only when confidence is low at save time. If the answer is not immediately clear from attached evidence, existing WTA/WI results, or memory, search it immediately rather than hypothesizing, asking the user to verify things manually, or proceeding on an unverified assumption. The 3/5 confidence hard stop remains a separate mandatory gate at save time. Root cause: CS02446542 (September 2026) — multiple turns were spent hypothesizing about AH_PostToGL, Sub-Ledger Take-Up, and GLD mechanisms before a WTG search immediately identified ACE as the relevant service task; the search should have been run at the first point of uncertainty about the mechanism.

EXTERNAL ONLINE CHECK — KNOWLEDGE BASE CONTENT IS NOT EXTERNAL: WiseTech Academy (WTA), MyAccount content, ACE Supplementary External Content, and ediProd materials (incidents, work items, knowledge articles) are internal WiseTech knowledge base content accessed via the `mcp_mcp-knowledge_*` and `mcp_mcp-ediprod_*` tools — they are NOT "external URLs" for the purposes of the EXTERNAL ONLINE CHECK rule or the EXTERNAL URLS CHECKED closing line. Only facts from sources genuinely outside WiseTech/CargoWise (government authority sites, carrier portals, third-party software such as Microsoft, etc.) trigger the EXTERNAL ONLINE CHECK requirement. When no genuine third-party sites were fetched via browser or fetch tools during an investigation, write `EXTERNAL URLS CHECKED: NONE`. Root cause: CS02438224 (August 2026) — a WTA article URL was incorrectly listed under EXTERNAL URLS CHECKED; it had been accessed via `mcp_mcp-knowledge_get-document-by-id`, not fetched externally; the correct closing line was `EXTERNAL URLS CHECKED: NONE`.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — CLIENT PREMISE ACCEPTED AS INVESTIGATION FRAME: When a client says "X works for declaration type A so it should work for type B," verify whether X is valid for type B before investigating a product gap. Do not adopt the client's assumption as the working hypothesis. Root cause: CS02397377 (July 2026) — client said H1 FR1 works fine and implied H5 should too; investigation adopted that frame and looked for a product gap instead of checking whether PVA is valid for H5 at all.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — COMPLETE FEATURE ABSENCE: REGISTRATION/CONFIGURATION VS. SECURITY: When a client reports a CargoWise menu option, tab, or feature is completely absent (not visible at all), do not default to security role as the primary hypothesis. In CargoWise, security denial typically renders features visible but blocked with an error when accessed — complete absence is more consistent with: (a) a missing feature registration (e.g. branch not registered for OCM with eHub via CR9 eRequest), (b) a missing module license, (c) a missing configuration prerequisite, or (d) the user having toggled tab visibility off using the View menu available on CargoWise records (the View menu allows individual tabs to be shown or hidden per user; always check and mention this as a possible cause in client-facing responses where a tab is reported absent). Before recommending a security investigation, establish whether security denial for that specific feature hides it entirely or shows it with an error. If the documented or precedented behavior is "show with error," complete absence eliminates security as the primary cause — investigate registration, configuration, and the View menu first. Root cause: CS02405626 (July 2026) — client reported Electronic Messaging > Carrier tab completely absent; first-pass response defaulted to security role as the cause; branch OCM registration with eHub (via CR9) and the View menu were identified only on the second pass.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — WEB PORTAL SECURITY MODEL ASSUMPTION: When investigating an access or security issue in a CargoWise web portal (TWH Desktop, TWH Mobile, Neo Staff Portal, or similar), do not assume the portal enforces security identically to CW1 desktop. Portals may have their own role layer configured within the portal itself, may evaluate CW1 security rights independently of portal roles, and may treat administrator flags (such as Is Controller) differently to CW1 desktop. Before forming any diagnosis, run a WTA search to confirm the specific security model for that portal — what it enforces, what CW1 rights it evaluates, and what administrator flags do or do not bypass portal-level checks. Root cause: CS02415808 (July 2026) — investigation assumed TWH Desktop portal security was configured via CW1 groups in the same way as desktop security; the portal has a two-layer model where portal roles are configured within the portal itself and CW1 Print To rights are evaluated independently; the error was not corrected until the user challenged the foundational assumption.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — COMPARATIVE ACCESS ANALYSIS: SUPERSET USER LOGIC: When comparing two users' access where one can and one cannot perform an action, first establish what rights the restricted user inherits from any groups or roles shared with the unrestricted user. If the restricted user holds all of the unrestricted user's groups plus additional ones, the access difference cannot be explained by divergent group membership — it must be explained by a configuration gap that affects all members of the shared groups (e.g. a resource with no rights configured in any group), or by a user-level override. Do not attribute an access gap to the extra groups or roles the restricted user holds when they are a superset of the unrestricted user's configuration. Root cause: CS02415808 (July 2026) — Alberto had all of Xavier's groups plus two more; the comparison paragraph incorrectly implied the extra groups were the cause of the access gap; the correct diagnosis was that PRTITZQ630-TEST had no Print To right configured in any group, including the shared ones.

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — PRIOR CLIENT ARGUMENT NOT REVIEWED: When a client cites a specific documented rule to argue the behavior is a defect, retrieve the prior incident conversation directly using `mcp_ediprod_get-job-details` and read it — do not rely on chatbot summaries, auto-suggested content, or incident metadata alone. If the client raised the same argument in a prior incident and it was not confirmed or refuted at the time, treat that argument as unresolved evidence carrying forward into the current investigation. Do not inherit a prior support non-escalation outcome as a resolved finding.

### eAdaptor / Automated Imports

~AD USER — NO FIXED STAFF RECORD OR DEPARTMENT: The `~AD` account is the internal system identity used for automated eAdaptor/native XML imports (XUB, Universal XML, etc.). It has NO conventional staff record in Staff and Resources — searching for Code starting with `~AD` returns no records. This is by design. `~AD` does NOT hold a fixed Home Branch or Home Department. The department used during import is resolved at import time from registry-configured department defaults, login context fallback, or workflow/automation rules — it cannot be pinpointed to a single UI screen or staff record. When investigating an import validation error where the "Created Department" does not match the expected value, do NOT instruct the client to check ~AD's Staff and Resources record — that record does not exist. Instead, investigate branch/department defaulting registry settings or the relevant XUB update note. WTA references: automated native XML import via ~AD - https://wisetechacademy.com/search?quickstart=6b97ac77-9181-42df-bcb2-fcb137bba3b4; XUB Branch and Department Defaulting Enhancement - https://wisetechacademy.com/search?quickstart=79808083-10e8-4a29-814f-82413ebc5e33. Confirmed by CS02436366 (August 2026).

### Database schema research

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — DISMISSED TABLE REVISIT: When searching for a CargoWise sub-table and searches for a dedicated table name return nothing, go back to any multi-purpose table already found (e.g. OrgRelatedParty) and test whether its discriminator column (e.g. PR_PartyType) covers the entity in question before continuing to search. Root cause: CS02403057 (July 2026) — OrgRelatedParty was found early in the Organizations PRG ERD but dismissed as "general related parties only"; subsequent searches for OrgAirCto/OAC_ failed; the answer was always OrgRelatedParty with PR_PartyType. Signal to watch for: a multi-purpose table has a discriminator/type column AND a WTA update note adds a field to the UI sub-tab that maps to a column already present on that table (e.g. "Direction" field added to Air CTO → PR_FreightDirection exists on OrgRelatedParty).

CARGOWISE VERIFIED TABLE — Organisation Port Related Parties (Air CTO, Sea CTO, Rail Head, etc.): All Port Related Parties entries are stored in OrgRelatedParty, distinguished by PR_PartyType. Confirmed by TAN WI00624649 (July 2023). Key columns: PR_OH_Parent (parent/carrier org FK → OH_PK), PR_OH_RelatedParty (CTO org FK → OH_PK), PR_PartyType (discriminator code), PR_FreightDirection (ARV/DEP/BTH). The PR_PartyType code for Air CTO is not published in user documentation — identify it by querying OrgRelatedParty against a known carrier with Air CTO configured.

### Aviation / CargoNaut

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — FWB ORIGIN AIRPORT VS AWB AUTOMATION STU CONTRADICTION: When investigating a CargoNaut or airline non-receipt issue, explicitly cross-reference the origin airport declared in the FWB AWB identification segment against any AWB Automation STU events in the W&T log that place the relevant flight at a different airport. If the STU event says a flight is at a different airport than the FWB declares as origin, that contradiction IS the likely root cause — the AWB origin is wrong — and must be resolved before pursuing CHAMP routing or OCI character hypotheses.

### UI panel and display issues

KNOWN FAILURE MODE — PANEL DIVIDER SIZING VS DPI REGRESSION: In CargoWise Forwarding Shipment screens (and other split-panel screens), the lower-right detail panel can be resized by dragging the divider between the grid and the detail area. This resize state is NOT controlled by the form layout template — resetting form layout does NOT restore it. If fields appear missing from the lower portion of a detail sub-panel, check whether the panel divider has been dragged to make the section too small BEFORE escalating as a DPI/scaling regression. Fix: drag the panel divider to resize the section larger. If a client has multiple monitors, also confirm all monitors are set to the same resolution and Windows display scaling percentage — a mismatch can cause CW1 windows to render with sections missing or mispositioned. Root cause: CS02453534 (September 2026).

### Client download URLs

For CargoWise client download guidance on self-hosted environments, always use https://myaccount.cargowise.com/Home/CargoWise/ClientDownloads.aspx.

For WiseCloud-hosted clients, the WebPrint Client installer is at `https://[wisecloudcode].webprint.wisegrid.net/client/CargoWiseOneWebPrintClientSetup.msi` (replace [wisecloudcode] with the client's WiseCloud code). Do NOT direct WiseCloud clients to MyAccount ClientDownloads.aspx — that is for self-hosted environments only.

COMPONENT VERSION ≠ CW BUILD VERSION: CargoWise components such as the WebPrint Client have their own user-visible version numbers (e.g., 7.108.0, visible in Windows Settings > Apps) separate from CargoWise DPR/GPR build numbers (e.g., 26.5.26.0). When describing an update to a client, use the component's own version number. Do not call a CW DPR build number a component "release version".

CWRDS PER-MACHINE DEPLOYMENT FOR ENTERPRISE ENVIRONMENTS: For globally-managed or multi-site environments where users do not have local admin rights, the CargoWise Remote Desktop Services (CWRDS) per-machine installation is the designed deployment path — it removes per-user upgrade prompts and puts IT in control of when updates are applied. Deploy `CargoWise.RemoteDesktopServices.msi` (available from https://myaccount.cargowise.com/Home/CargoWise/ClientDownloads.aspx) using: `msiexec.exe /i CargoWise.RemoteDesktopServices.msi ALLUSERS=1 MSIINSTALLPERUSER="" /l*v "C:\Temp\CargoWise.RemoteDesktopServices.Install-Permachine.log"`. Full SCCM/Intune deployment guidance — including the `PerMachineMigrate` registry flag (which prevents the CargoWise Cloud Accessor (WCA) from overriding an existing per-machine install with a per-user install during the migration period) — is in Update Note 20260703 - https://wisetechacademy.com/search?quickstart=db36c690-47c9-4396-8cfb-396cdd8f8e48. The "not installed" warning appears when WCA looks for a per-user entry under the user's local profile and cannot find it — a per-machine entry in Programs and Features alone does not satisfy this check in current WCA versions. WI00996343 (CLS) and Update Note 20260121d are the authoritative references for the per-user installer model change. Root cause: CS02438224 (August 2026) — client managing 200+ workstations globally asked about enterprise CWRDS upgrade management; per-machine MSI deployment is the designed path for this scenario.

### Escalation notes

When the user says `draft an escalation note`, treat it as: create an internal escalation summary that states the issue, lists the evidence already provided, explains why that evidence shows escalation is required, then save as `.txt` to the workspace folder without waiting for another prompt.

Internal escalation note formatting rule: use ALL CAPS section headings followed by a blank line and then prose body. Do NOT use `---` or `----` divider lines anywhere in escalation notes. No decorative separators of any kind.

ESCALATION NOTE — EXTERNAL URL CITATION RULE: If any external URLs were fetched during the investigation and those URLs contributed to the client-facing response (used to confirm root cause, support workaround recommendations, or shape the escalation rationale), include those URLs in an EXTERNAL SOURCES VERIFIED DURING INVESTIGATION section of the escalation note. URLs that were checked but did not contribute to the client response content do not need to be included. Root cause: CS02398126 (July 2026) — four external Microsoft sources confirmed the drag event payload regression and informed both the client response and the escalation note.

Do not upload client-facing responses or escalation notes to eDocs. Save them as `.txt` files in the workspace folder only — do not upload to the incident/workitem's eDocs unless the user explicitly asks for that as a one-off exception.

Never update, append, or add notes to Workflow Tasks unless the user explicitly overrides this rule.

Never post internal conversation messages (mcp_ediprod_send-conversation-message) on any incident, workitem, or project unless the user explicitly asks. Unsolicited internal notes are out of scope.

Never append to or update a workitem description (mcp_ediprod_update-workitem) unless the user explicitly asks. The same applies to incident and project record updates beyond what the defined workflow step authorises.

---

## Step 5 — Pre-Draft Audit (Run Before Writing the Draft)

Run all four parts of this audit and record the results before writing any draft text:

1. UI PATH AUDIT — List every CargoWise module name, menu path, screen label, and navigation sequence you plan to include. Confirm each is supported by a WTA search result, an authoritative document, or a directly reviewed screenshot. If a path is partially known from a non-WTA source, run a WTA search to verify and complete it. Remove any path that cannot be confirmed even after search.

2. EDIFACT MAPPING AUDIT — List every field change you plan to recommend to fix a specific EDIFACT segment output. For each one, run a WTA or WI search to confirm the current field-to-segment mapping is still active in the current product build. Do not proceed to draft if the mapping is unverified.

3. WORK ITEM CHECK — this is a confirmatory check: for every technical claim in the planned response about how a CargoWise feature works, why a behavior occurs, or what the correct output should be, run `mcp_ediprod_filter-workitems` (or a WTA search) to confirm the described behavior is current and has not been changed by a recent work item. If a relevant WI is found, incorporate it into the response (fixed build, workaround, or escalation as appropriate). Do not proceed to draft until this check is complete. This step verifies that the response claims are consistent with current product behavior — it is distinct from the POST-ATTACHMENT ROOT CAUSE GATE, which runs earlier in the investigation and asks "is this a known issue?" before any hypothesis is formed.

4. CONFIGURATION EXISTENCE AUDIT — For every specific CargoWise field, setting, or configuration step you plan to recommend as a fix, confirm it exists and is accessible in the product UI via a WTA article, a directly reviewed client screenshot, or prior verified product knowledge. Log output alone does not confirm a field exists as a configurable option. For steps involving a combination of field values, confirm the specific combination is valid — not just each field individually.

---

## Step 6 — Response Style

- The response must be client-facing and ready to paste directly into the eRequest.
- Start with: Hi [Contact First Name], — address the most recent active client correspondent in the eConversation thread, not automatically the original reporter. Determine the first name from the author identifier of the most recent non-WiseTech eConversation post: if it is a full email address, strip the domain (e.g. jim.goin@efwnow.com → jim.goin), split on the first period (jim.goin → jim), capitalize (Jim). If the identifier cannot be parsed to a recognizable first name, fall back to the original reporter's first name from the Reported by field on the incident.
- Use business-appropriate language and clear paragraph spacing.
- Do not use internal-handoff wording such as "please request the customer".
- KNOWN FAILURE MODE — CROSS-CLIENT ERESQUEST NUMBER IN CLIENT-FACING TEXT: Never name another organisation's eRequest/incident number (e.g. "CS02308551") in the client-facing body of a response, even when citing it only as a precedent for an identical error string with no other client detail disclosed. A different client's incident number is confidential to that client and must never appear before the "THE BELOW IS FOR INFORMATION ONLY" separator. State the product/error behavior directly instead without the case number. An eRequest number belonging to the SAME client/org as the current incident is fine to reference in the body. Cross-client incident numbers are only appropriate in the internal "Similar incidents" footer section, below the separator. Root cause: CS02450914 (September 2026) — a different, unrelated org's incident number was named in the client-facing body of a response; caught by the user, who noted this had never been done before.
- ONE ISSUE PER ERQUEST: An eRequest can only handle one issue at a time. When an incident description raises a second, distinct issue alongside the primary one being investigated, do not investigate or request diagnostic evidence for the secondary issue in the same response. Instead, briefly note that it should be raised as its own separate eRequest if the client needs help with it, and do not include any diagnostic questions or evidence requests for that secondary issue in the current response. Root cause: CS02450914 (September 2026) — a response asked for job numbers/field details to investigate a secondary issue mentioned in the same incident as the primary one; eRequests are one-issue-only and the secondary issue should be deferred to its own eRequest instead.
- Prefers a clear business tone with direct answers and concrete reasoning from evidence — moderate detail rather than overly short replies.
- In client-facing prose, state supported product behavior directly from the current evidence and authoritative sources. Avoid wording that presents the conclusion as coming from similar incidents, support precedents, or other case comparisons.
- KNOWN FAILURE MODE — DOCUMENTATION ATTRIBUTION PHRASING: Do not use attribution phrases that place a source between the reader and the product fact — e.g., "CargoWise documentation confirms that...", "According to WTA...", "The WTA article states...", "As per the update note...". State the product behavior directly as fact: "The Job Closure Date recognition style does not generate WIPs or Accruals." The inline URL citation is still required in the same sentence; only the framing must be direct rather than attributed.
- When referencing any Update Note, WiseTech Academy article, FAQ, how-to, reference guide, or other eLearning content in the response body, include the direct URL inline in the same sentence using the format: `<title or description> - <url>`. A URL placed only in the footer does NOT satisfy this requirement — the inline citation and the footer listing are both required independently.
- KNOWN FAILURE MODE — INLINE URL OMISSION: WTA references have been written into the response body as plain text without an inline URL. Before finalizing, scan every sentence in the response body that names or describes a WTA article or guide and confirm it contains an inline URL.
- KNOWN FAILURE MODE — UNREAD WTA CITATION: A WTA URL included in a response body must have been read (document content retrieved via mcp_wtgkb_get-document-by-id and the capability verified from the content) before it is cited. Including a WTA link that was not read constitutes an unverified recommendation, regardless of what the tool name or article title implies. An article title that sounds relevant is NOT the same as a read article confirming the capability. The CONFIGURATION EXISTENCE CHECK in the pre-save scan must include, for every cited WTA URL: "was the document content retrieved and read as part of this investigation?" If no, retrieve and read it before finalizing. Root cause: CS02410011 (July 2026) — the Workflow Diagnostic Screen URL (cfff6738) was cited as the tool for identifying affected org records; the document was not read until the follow-up question; the article confirmed the tool is a per-record diagnostic with no cross-org capability, directly contradicting the response claim.
- KNOWN FAILURE MODE — WTA ARTICLE MARKED AS INTERNAL ONLY: When a WTA document is retrieved via `mcp_mcp-knowledge_get-document-by-id`, check the `File_Content` field for the string "(WiseTech Global Internal Only)". If present, the article is restricted to WiseTech staff and must NOT be cited in a client-facing response — neither as an inline URL in the response body nor in the WTA footer. This check is required for every article retrieved before it is used in a response. If the only source confirming a recommended action is marked internal-only: (a) search for a publicly available WTA reference on the same topic using `search-knowledge-many-results`; (b) if no public reference exists, describe the feature or capability without citing the article — do not include the internal-only URL in any part of the client-facing text. Root cause: CS02446542 (August 2026) — the "Re-generate Accounting Transaction Journal Entries" Update Note (da1483c8) was cited inline and in the WTA footer of the initial draft; the `File_Content` field contained "(WiseTech Global Internal Only)" in the document header; the URL had to be removed after manual review.
- Do not use ALL CAPS section subheadings anywhere in the response body.
- Do not use bold or title-case section headers (e.g., "What the logs reveal", "Monitoring rejected EDI messages") anywhere in the response body. Write the response as flowing paragraphs with transitional prose, not a document with titled sections.
- Do not use `---` horizontal rule dividers anywhere in the response text, including as separators between body sections or between the body and footer content.
- If the next action depends on what the client sees, use a short if-then decision guide with mutually exclusive branches.
- REDUNDANT QUESTION AFTER IF/THEN COVERAGE: If the response body already covers both branches of a conditional decision with full resolution steps for each branch (e.g. eAdaptor Next → EDI Client Staff Proxy; Legacy → registry Proxy Users setting), do NOT add a closing question asking the client to confirm which branch applies. The if/then structure is self-contained. Adding the question makes the response appear incomplete and creates unnecessary friction for the client. Root cause: CS02381555 (July 2026) — after presenting both resolution paths with complete instructions, the response asked the client to confirm which integration channel they use.
- Before finalizing the client-facing response, do a wording pass to remove habit-driven hedges and rewrite any evidence-backed conclusion as a direct statement from the current documentation or verified evidence.
- NO REPEAT ANSWERS: Before finalising a response, scan every question or topic addressed in the response body against all prior conversation posts in the incident thread. If a question was already answered in a prior response and the client's latest message does not specifically ask a follow-up about it, remove it from the current response. Root cause: CS02383547 (July 2026) — the Update Note documentation question was answered in the July 9 13:22 response; Romain's July 9 14:33 re-open did not mention it, but the next response included a paragraph on it anyway.
- Sign off with:

Thank You,
[Current user's first name]

Determine the current user's first name from the workspace path or VS Code user data path visible in context. These paths follow the pattern `C:\Users\<windows_username>\...`. Extract the `<windows_username>` segment (e.g., `james.edstrom`), take the text before the first period, and capitalize the first letter (e.g., `james` → `James`). If the username contains no period, capitalize the full username. Use this name on the sign-off line for every response.

After the sign-off, leave two blank lines, then insert the following line in ALL CAPS:

THE BELOW IS FOR INFORMATION ONLY, DO NOT SEND TO CLIENT

Leave one blank line after this separator before the confidence rating.

---

## Step 7 — Required Footer Content

Add each section below in the listed order, with exactly one empty line between each:

1. Confidence rating on its own line in exactly this format: `Confidence: X/5` — no inline explanation or rationale text after the number.

2. Exactly this disclaimer line: `DISCLAIMER FOR WISETECH SUPPORT - This response was generated by an AI agent and may not be correct. Please review before acting.`

3. Up to 5 similar or related incidents from the last 3 years. Each bullet must include: incident number, a short title, a brief description of the problem, and the resolution outcome — not just the incident number, title, and status metadata tuple.

4. A section headed exactly: `Relevant WiseTech Academy links:`
   - In that section, list up to 5 genuinely relevant wisetechacademy.com items using this exact per-line format: `- <module title> - <url>`. Use a hyphen with spaces ( - ) between the title and URL, not an em dash.
   - Do not repeat in the academy footer any URL already cited inline in the response body.
   - Do not output bare academy URLs without the corresponding module title.
   - If no genuinely relevant academy content is identified, state that explicitly under the same heading instead of listing generic links.

---

## Step 8 — Pre-Save Scan Gate

Before calling any file-creation tool to write the response .txt file, explicitly confirm in chat that all five checks pass. The .txt file must not be created until every check below is explicitly confirmed passed in chat:

1. INLINE URL CHECK — Read every sentence in the response body that names or describes a WiseTech Academy article, Update Note, how-to, FAQ, reference guide, or other eLearning content. Confirm each sentence contains the URL inline using the format `<title or description> - <url>`. Fix any omission in the draft before proceeding. A URL placed only in the footer does not satisfy this check.

2. FORMATTING CHECK — Confirm there are no bold or title-case section headers, no `---` horizontal rule dividers, and no ALL CAPS subheadings anywhere in the response body.

3. FOOTER COMPLETENESS CHECK — Confirm the sign-off is `Thank You,` followed by the current user's first name; confirm the THE BELOW IS FOR INFORMATION ONLY separator line is present after the sign-off; the confidence rating line is exactly `Confidence: X/5` with no inline explanation after the number; each similar incident entry contains a description and resolution outcome (not just metadata); and no URL already cited inline in the response body is repeated in the academy footer section.

4. KNOWN FAILURE MODE SCAN — Explicitly state in chat whether each of the following failure modes was applicable to this response and how it was handled: UI path fabrication risk; WTA how-to path abbreviation risk; WTA how-to wrong top-level menu risk; configuration inference from log or behavior risk; tab visibility does not confirm tab contents risk; field combination validity risk; registry mechanism scope assumption risk; caveat bypass risk; hedged behavior claim not verified risk; conditional option applicability verification risk; EDIFACT segment-to-field mapping assumption risk; inline URL omission risk; unread WTA citation risk; WTA UI path/tab label not diffed against already-reviewed screenshot risk; WTA article marked as internal only risk; documentation attribution phrasing risk; defect misclassification as expected behavior risk; prior client argument not reviewed risk; external online check not performed risk; fabricated external URLs risk; live URL reachability check not performed risk; client premise accepted as investigation frame risk; complete feature absence: registration/configuration vs. security risk; web portal security model assumption risk; comparative access analysis: superset user logic risk; log evidence for one entity does not cover another risk; WI mechanism not verified in attachment evidence risk; high-volume WI with low customer report rate accepted as root cause risk; closed sibling WI not checked risk; WI dismissed on title without checking attached incidents risk; WI attachment rule: loose WI match escalated to product team rather than attached as incident link risk; causal inference to explain observed state risk; causal inference sentence-level trigger risk (guessed mechanism presented as fact, or any guessed mechanism presented in a client response at all even if hedged); mechanism claim not re-checked against its own specific precondition in already-attached evidence risk; client response vs escalation note inference bar risk; negative capability claim not verified risk; office document caption direction assumption risk (for any DOCX/XLSX/PDF with interleaved images and text, confirm caption direction was established via structural check + verification before interpreting images). For any that applied, confirm the verification step was completed before the draft was written.

5. CONFIGURATION EXISTENCE CHECK — For every specific CargoWise field, setting, or configuration step recommended as a fix, state in chat what source (WTA article URL, reviewed screenshot, or prior verified product knowledge) confirms it exists and is accessible in the product UI. For steps involving a combination of field values, confirm the specific combination is valid — not just each field individually. Log output alone does not satisfy this check. Tab visibility in a screenshot alone does NOT confirm what fields are on a tab — tab contents must be confirmed via a WTA article describing those fields or a screenshot showing the tab's interior.

6. EXTERNAL URL LINE CHECK — If any external URL fetch failed during the investigation, confirm that a separate `EXTERNAL URL COULD NOT BE PARSED: <urls>` line is present in the planned completion check output. Do NOT accept an inline status note within the EXTERNAL URLS CHECKED line as a substitute. If any fetch failed and this separate line is missing, add it before creating the .txt file.

---

## Step 9 — Save and Completion Check

- Save the final client-facing response as a .txt file to the designated workspace output folder.
- COMPLETION CHECK GATE — FILE READ TRACKING TABLE MUST BE RESOLVED: This completion check cannot be satisfied by memory or impression alone. Before writing "attachments successfully reviewed" or `FILES COULD NOT BE PARSED: NONE`, re-open the MANDATORY FILE READ TRACKING TABLE produced earlier and confirm every row shows READ, not PENDING. Any row still PENDING must either be resolved with a follow-up `read_file` call before the final response is written, or the file must be named explicitly in the `FILES COULD NOT BE PARSED:` line — it cannot simply be dropped from both.
- Before the final chat response to the user, run a mandatory completion check covering:
  - Attachments successfully reviewed
  - Attachments that could not be parsed/viewed (FILES COULD NOT BE PARSED: <comma-separated file names>)
  - Whether any conclusion depends on unresolved evidence
  - Whether every UI path in the response was validated
  - Whether every recommended configuration step was confirmed to exist in the product UI by a WTA article, reviewed screenshot, or verified product knowledge (not inferred from log output)
  - Whether every recommended field change was verified against a current EDIFACT mapping source
  - Whether the Work Item check was completed for all technical claims in the response
  - Whether every WiseTech Academy article, Update Note, how-to, FAQ, or other eLearning content referenced in the response body has its URL included inline in the same sentence
  - A list of every external URL fetched during the investigation (successful or failed)

- Always include exactly one `FILES COULD NOT BE PARSED:` line in the final chat response. Write `FILES COULD NOT BE PARSED: NONE` if all files and all embedded images were successfully parsed and reviewed; write `FILES COULD NOT BE PARSED: <specific files or image ranges>` if any failed. Never omit this line.
- FLAG PARTIAL FAILURES, NOT JUST WHOLE-FILE FAILURES: The FILES COULD NOT BE PARSED line covers any content that could not be parsed for any reason — a whole file, a subset of pages, specific embedded images, a truncated document, an ambiguous/unreadable region of an image, or any other partial gap — not only outright whole-file failures. The only standing exception is SystemReport .zip files, which are deliberately excluded per policy and not treated as a parse failure. If any part of anything was not fully consumed, name that specific part in the line (e.g. "DOCX_1 images 04-09", "page 3 of Evidence.pdf illegible") rather than omitting it because the rest of the file parsed fine.
- If any external URL fetch failed or returned unreadable content during the investigation, include exactly one line in the final chat response: `EXTERNAL URL COULD NOT BE PARSED: <comma-separated URLs>`.
- Never omit the EXTERNAL URL COULD NOT BE PARSED line merely because the client-facing response correctly excludes it.
- In the final chat response, include a line listing all external URLs that were successfully fetched during the investigation: `EXTERNAL URLS CHECKED: <comma-separated URLs>`, or `EXTERNAL URLS CHECKED: NONE` if no external fetches were performed.
- EXTERNAL URL COULD NOT BE PARSED — MANDATORY SEPARATE LINE: These two URL lines are SEPARATE required output lines — do NOT collapse both into a single `EXTERNAL URLS CHECKED` line with inline status notes (e.g. "(404)" or "(failed)"). If all fetches succeeded, omit the EXTERNAL URL COULD NOT BE PARSED line entirely. The Step 8 pre-save scan must confirm the EXTERNAL URL COULD NOT BE PARSED line is present as its own line whenever any fetch failed. Root cause: CS02418951 (July 2026) — the 404 on the service-codes URL was noted inline in EXTERNAL URLS CHECKED but the mandatory separate EXTERNAL URL COULD NOT BE PARSED warning line was not written.
